one_month_reasoning: In-window events: (1) the Oct 27-28 FOMC, decision Oct 28, with ~69% hike odds on Kalshi/Polymarket as of Sep 29 (per supervisor, defirate/CNBC); a hike is largely priced, so it adds variance to a high-beta semi rather than a clear drift, though a surprise hold would help and a hawkish path hurts; (2) the broad price adjustment effective Oct 10 (Sep 16 customer notice per distributor; management confirmed at the Aug 27 Deutsche Bank conference that a second price increase is underway), mildly positive but known; (3) late-October peer prints (TI, NXP, STMicro) that move the analog/power group either way. onsemi's own Q3 report is estimated ~Nov 2 (MarketBeat/Alpha Vantage, not confirmed), just outside the window, with a small chance it lands inside. Short interest eased to 7.62% of float (Sep 15), no squeeze setup. No directional edge: near-symmetric lognormal with median ~$75.8 and ~18% monthly vol (64%/3.5), a touch wider in the tails than round 1 for the FOMC and the small chance of an in-window print.

fair_value.method: Blend of 17x skeptic NTM EPS of $4.55 (= $77) at 60% weight and a 5% FCF yield on capex-normalised forward FCF of ~$1.55B (= $77) at 40% weight, giving ~$77.

Cyclical auto/industrial semi with ~7.6% short float and China SiC competition; 5% sits between trough (6-7%) and peak (3-4%) cycle valuations.

bear.story: Auto/industrial recovery stalls, the October price increases fail to stick once supply loosens, utilisation stalls in the 80s, Chinese SiC (~$400 vs ~$1,200/wafer) crushes SiC pricing, and a Fed hiking cycle compresses semi multiples; CY27 EPS ~$3.2 on ~14x, plus Synaptics dilution and integration noise from mid-2027. Revisits the 52-week low area.

base.story: Margins recover toward 41-42% GM as utilisation climbs and pricing lands; CY27 EPS ~$4.2-4.5; AI-DC grows but the 2030 roadmap is not paid for in advance; Synaptics closes mid-2027 roughly EPS-neutral; multiple holds ~17x.

bull.story: Tight supply, two price increases and utilisation toward 92% drive upside revisions; 800V DC AI content visible; CY28 EPS path >$5.2 and the market re-rates to 22-23x, retracing toward the June high.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$50 (about 11x CY27 consensus, roughly a 7-8% yield on capex-normalised FCF, ~34% below spot, near the Mar-Apr 2026 range) the price would most likely reflect a genuine earnings reset: a Q3/Q4 guide-down from auto/industrial demand, the price increases reversing, an SiC price war hitting device margins, or a failed/renegotiated Synaptics deal, rather than ordinary volatility in a 64%-vol stock.

reasoning: Skeptic lane, round 2. Supervisor found no factual errors in my round-1 numbers, confirmed net debt ~$0.595B and consensus CY26/CY27 $3.20/$4.53, and flagged (a) the Oct 10 price increase rested on a distributor blog, (b) my 10% EPS haircut may double-count SiC pressure already in an upward-revised consensus, (c) FCF legs built on trough capex, and (d) the Oct 28 FOMC in the 1-month window. Follow-ups: management at the Aug 27 Deutsche Bank conference confirmed an April increase and a second increase underway, and cited utilisation 68% -> 83% with 25-30bp GM per point up to ~92% and capex at mid-single-digit intensity; TD Cowen's Jun 26 downgrade (Buy->Hold, $110) was about valuation (~25x its 2027 estimate at the time), consumer/wireless exposure (~60% of Synaptics), EPS reliance on loadings, and accretion only in 2028-29; post-analyst-day target cuts (Stifel and Truist to $75, Wells $85, Cantor $90) sit well below the stale $103.69 mean; the Aug 7 round of cuts was multiple compression, not estimate cuts (BofA raised CY27 EPS 7%); CFO sold 90k shares Apr 2026, no new insider sales found; short float fell to 7.62% (Sep 15); no credit-rating or covenant stress found. Net: I narrow the EPS haircut to ~6% (partly double-counted), which lifts the P/E leg to $77, but normalising capex cuts the FCF leg from $85 to $77, so fair value falls slightly from $79 to $77. I disagree with nothing the supervisor established; I keep my own multiple (17x) and FCF yield (5%). Scenarios 22/53/25 at $45/$78/$120 (mean ~$81, median ~$77). Ladder: lognormal around a ~$76.5 median at ~50-52% vol with a fattened left tail; slightly less left-tail weight than round 1 since the price increase and utilisation gains are now primary-sourced, offset by the hiking Fed. Research remains limited: no primary TD Cowen note or credit-agency report reachable, and onsemi's own price notice text was not found (only management's conference confirmation).
